## Technology profile: versions 2 and 3 {#technology-profile-v2-v3}

*In progress.* Versions 2 and 3 score **every** OpenAlex topic (4,516) and **every** CPC main group (9,867)
for each Engine by embedding similarity to the grant text (SPECTER2 for topics, PatentSBERTa for CPC), so
that nothing is left out by hand. They differ only in the input: v2 uses every sentence of the grant title
and abstract; v3 uses only the science and technology fragments extracted from them, word for word, with a
fixed prompt. Version 1 (below) was an earlier manual choice and is shown for reference, not as a
benchmark. Version 3.1 (planned) completes version 3: it adds the selection step, which neither v2 nor v3
has yet, and fixes the problems found in the review of their rankings. The diagram labels are in Russian.

### Versions compared {#versions-compared}

::: {.no-sort}

| Step | v1 (on this site) | v2 | v3 | v3.1 (planned) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Source | NSF grant title and abstract | same | same | same |
| Splitting into technologies | by hand: 3-5 statements per Engine (48 in total), each with a verbatim quote | none: every sentence on its own, including sentences on the region and workforce | none: 123 science and technology fragments extracted with a fixed prompt, checked to be verbatim | fragments from a revised prompt (no industries of application, no generic qualities such as "resilience"), each labelled with one of the grant's 3-5 technologies |
| Candidates: OpenAlex topics | top 3 of the OpenAlex `/text/topics` classifier per statement | all 4,516 topics | same | same |
| Candidates: CPC | chosen by hand; subclasses (C22B) and main groups (B29B17) mixed | all 9,867 main groups (subclass and group titles) | same | all main groups, with the titles of their first-level subgroups; indexing groups (2000+, /99) dropped or down-weighted |
| Scoring | classifier score; no score for CPC | embedding cosine (SPECTER2 for topics, PatentSBERTa for CPC), mean-centred; the Engine's name masked as "the Engine" | same | same, with "Engine" removed rather than inserted (PatentSBERTa reads it as a motor) |
| Selection | the classifier's first topic, sometimes the second by hand, with a stated reason | not done: rankings only | not done: rankings only | per technology, near-duplicates removed (MMR); **core**: 2-3 topics and 2-3 CPC codes per technology, checked by eye; **broad profile**: everything above one relevance threshold, with no limit on the number of CPC codes |
| Check against data | patents per CPC code (US and region, 2024-25), so that no code is empty | none | none | share of the team's works and patents in the profile; coverage of US patents; metrics for both the core and the broad profile |
| Status | used for all metrics on this site | rankings done | rankings done | planned |

:::

The profile describes what the grant says the Engine does. Data are used only to check it, not to choose it:
choosing codes by the number of regional patents would make the region's Patent LQ high by construction.

### Classification lists

Both lists are public and are kept in the repository as CSV files (`data/reference/`, downloaded by
`py/00_reference_lists.py`):

- **OpenAlex topics**: all 4,516 topics of the OpenAlex topic classification, with their descriptions and
  keywords, from the [OpenAlex topics API](https://api.openalex.org/topics)
  ([documentation](https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/topics)). OpenAlex gives the list no version
  number; every topic has the creation date January 2024 in the API. Downloaded on November 15, 2026.
- **CPC titles**: the title list of the Cooperative Patent Classification, scheme 2026.08
  ([CPCTitleList202608.zip](https://www.cooperativepatentclassification.org/sites/default/files/cpc/bulk/CPCTitleList202608.zip),
  from the [CPC bulk download page](https://www.cooperativepatentclassification.org/cpcSchemeAndDefinitions/bulk)):
  every section, class, subclass, main group and subgroup with its official title (254,314 codes, of them
  9,867 main groups). The CPC site labels this list "CPC Title List (2026.08)"; its files are dated
  August 1, 2026. Downloaded on November 15, 2026.

## Technology profile, version 1 {#technology-profile}

The technology profile states what each Engine works on in two vocabularies: OpenAlex topics (for papers) and
CPC classes (for patents). It is built from the text of the NSF grant itself, not from the Engine's website.

1. **Statements.** Each Engine gets 3-5 short statements about its technology. The first always comes from
   the grant title (the acronym expanded from the abstract; IMPACT's title is not informative, which is noted).
   The others come from the technical part of the NSF abstract. Every statement keeps a verbatim quote.
   File: `data/manual/tech_statements.csv`.
2. **OpenAlex topics.** Each statement is classified on its own with the OpenAlex `/text/topics` classifier
   ($0.01 per call). Whole abstracts are not classified: the full NEO-SMART abstract gets the topic
   "Regional resilience and development", which describes the programme, not the technology. The top three
   candidates are kept; rank 1 is used unless `data/manual/tech_topic_choice.csv` records another choice with
   its reason (`r nrow(choices)` cases).
3. **CPC classes.** CPC codes are chosen by hand for each statement, at subclass level (e.g. C22B) or main
   group (B29B17), and checked against USPTO grants of 2024-2025: patents with the code in the whole US and
   with an inventor in the Engine's states. A code with almost no patents in the region shows up at once.
4. **How the profile is used.** A paper is *in the Engine's topics* when at least one of its three OpenAlex
   topics is a profile topic. A patent is *in the profile* when at least one of its CPC codes is a profile code.
   These give the regional patents in the profile, the location quotient (LQ) and the comparison with US states.

In total: `r n_distinct(profile$engine_name)` Engines, `r nrow(profile)` statements
(`r sum(profile$source == "title")` from titles, `r sum(profile$source == "abstract")` from abstracts).

### Profile of each Engine

```{r profile-tables, results = "asis"}
engines <- sort(unique(profile$engine_name))
cat('<select id="profile-engine" class="form-control" style="width:auto; margin-bottom:10px">\n',
    paste0('<option value="', seq_along(engines), '">', esc(engines), "</option>", collapse = "\n"),
    "\n</select>\n\n")
# "C22B; C22C" + "C22B:688; C22C:2757" + "C22B:10; C22C:61" -> "C22B (688 / 10)<br>C22C (2757 / 61)"
fmt_cpc <- function(cpc, us, reg) {
  if (is.na(cpc)) return("")
  codes <- str_split_1(cpc, ";\\s*")
  counts <- function(x) { v <- str_split_1(coalesce(x, ""), ";\\s*")
                          setNames(str_extract(v, "\\d+$"), str_remove(v, ":.*$")) }
  n_us <- counts(us); n_reg <- counts(reg)
  paste(sprintf("%s (%s / %s)", codes, coalesce(n_us[codes], "?"), coalesce(n_reg[codes], "?")), collapse = "<br>")
}
for (k in seq_along(engines)) {
  p <- profile |> filter(engine_name == engines[k]) |> arrange(item)
  tab <- tibble(`#` = p$item,
                Source = p$source,
                Statement = esc(p$statement),
                `Quote from the grant` = paste0("<i>", esc(str_trunc(coalesce(p$quote, ""), 220)), "</i>"),
                `OpenAlex topic (subfield)` = paste0(esc(p$topic), "<br><span style='color:#666'>",
                                                     esc(p$subfield), "</span>"),
                `CPC (US / region patents, 2024-25)` = mapply(fmt_cpc, p$cpc, p$cpc_patents_us_2024_25,
                                                              p$cpc_patents_region_2024_25))
  cat(sprintf('<div class="profile-engine" data-k="%d"%s>\n', k, if (k > 1) ' style="display:none"' else ""))
  print(kable(tab, format = "html", escape = FALSE, table.attr = 'class="table table-condensed"'))
  cat("</div>\n\n")
}
```

<script>
// Dropdown: show the chosen Engine's profile table
document.getElementById("profile-engine").addEventListener("change", function () {
  var k = this.value;
  document.querySelectorAll(".profile-engine").forEach(function (d) {
    d.style.display = d.getAttribute("data-k") === k ? "" : "none";
  });
});
</script>
